title: Permanent server rejection of a save has no terminal path — silent indefinite retry (client email gate is looser than shared/email.is_valid)
detail: An applicant whose plausible-looking email passes the client regex but fails the server's stricter rule gets zero draft persistence with no signal, and the dead POST repeats on every step change/beacon. Only closed:true has a terminal state; other permanent rejections retry forever.
recommended_fix: Mirror the shared rule client-side (or accept the server's verdict): treat an ok:false/4xx that is not closed as terminal for this payload — suppress further saves until a field actually changes, or give up after N identical rejections.

title: Capability gate doesn't cover Promise.prototype.finally, but the continue-button chain ends in .finally
detail: Browsers with fetch/CustomEvent/JSON but no Promise.prototype.finally (Edge 14–17, Safari 10.1–11.0) pass the gate, then the click handler throws synchronously constructing the chain (.finally is not a function): the button stays disabled, no status copy appears — while the fetch itself has already fired.
recommended_fix: Add Promise.prototype.finally to the capability gate, or replace .finally with re-enabling the button inside both the .then and .catch arms.
